set.body:
Current release queue, 7 October 2026: release-1.0; milestone-inputs.
Plan: docs/refactor/RELEASE-QUEUE.md. Mote remains authoritative; one primary agent and at most one helper.

Reconciliation: Acceptance retained; this audit did not run its proposed tests.

Remaining / next action: Build ordinary-file source/cohort preparation over existing text, annotation, recall timing and checked source contracts. Preserve source edition, participants/sessions, optional times and failed-subject independence; expose readiness without automatic cloud/model fallback.

Release tags schedule work; they do not establish completion or empirical qualification. Use current AGENTS.md for ownership, scoped gates and exact-SHA review; old fleet roles, timers and fixed gate task counts are historical. Keep the original scientific preregistration, denominators, admission and sealed-test rules below.

Retained acceptance and design context:

Owner requirement, 22 September 2026: StoryModel provides the path from ordinary user inputs to the correct checked artifacts for StoryAtlas. Governing producer workflow: docs/plans/2026-09-22-recall-encoding-workflow.md sections 2 and 8. Detailed researcher entry contract: sibling storyatlas4s/docs/delivery/workspace-design.md section 8.0. This is production intake, not the fixture-only generator in M1.

Reuse and scope: extend existing pipeline/StoryPipeline, source acquisition/corpus-intake adapters, canonical codecs and stable recall inventory/timing. Inspect and reuse existing Unicode source/surface work bd-01M1998654XQRSNA6R16S2ABDQ instead of reviving its historical WOG-only assumptions. Keep corpus column/path adapters outside solver and viewer; no new top-level module or bench import.

Acceptance:
1. A documented minimal study config or ordinary CLI arguments identify original source text or movie/source-annotation files, one or more recall transcript paths, participant/session IDs, explicit profile and output location. The user never supplies internal Address values, checksums, canonical JSON joins or handwritten output manifests. Provide a template and validate/preview command; exact command names are fixed by implementation.
2. Prepare/freeze the source once and import every recall independently. Support UTF-8 untimed text plus explicitly documented timed/tabular adapters. Preserve original bytes/canonicalization lineage, Unicode, stable words, unit membership/segmentation identity, missing/onset-only/interval timing and per-file source association. Timestamps and recall audio are optional for ordinal inspection. Multiple sessions/duplicate filenames cannot alias participant identity.
3. Reuse a supplied checked source package where present. Annotation-assisted film preparation preserves time-aligned source descriptions and stated coverage. Dialogue subtitles are not complete visual scene descriptions; raw video plus recall text requires a supported configured source-perception/film route or an actionable missing-capability result. Never reconstruct the reference source from the subjects' recalls or invent source timing/semantic structure. Existing D1A-film/D1B obligations remain separate.
4. Readiness identifies required runtime/media/model assets or configured provider, explicit content destination/cost policy, and offline availability before execution. Missing local artifacts fail offline without automatic download/cloud fallback. Source-only preparation works without recall; a failed subject does not erase other prepared inventories.
5. Independent fixtures cover two untimed subjects, repeated sessions, malformed/foreign timing, changed source edition and missing video-analysis capability. Generated checked inputs decode through public APIs and preserve exact source/recall identity/support without manual repairs.

Evidence: exact input/config/output digests and producer revision; focused platform and failure/control tests, reference-scope for actual diff, SD6 separate review and applicable checkAll landing gate. This ticket creates checked inputs; mapping execution/config semantics remain in the existing public facade and canonical workspace publishing has its own child. No automatic-science/calibration claim. Rollback preserves existing storyBuild and corpus-specific readers while the new adapter refuses unsupported input.
